item.title: Leader’s sincere response to a Letter from a ten-year-old Student
item.description: Tehran, IRNA – Following a sincere and affectionate letter sent by a ten-year-old student from Tehran to the Leader of the Revolution; in response to the student’s expression of affection, Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei wrote a letter to the student and also presented a gift in return.
item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://en.irna.ir/news/86310543/Leader-s-sincere-response-to-a-Letter-from-a-ten-year-old-Student

Tehran, IRNA – Following a sincere and affectionate letter sent by a ten-year-old student from Tehran to the Leader of the Revolution; in response to the student’s expression of affection, Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei wrote a letter to the student and also presented a gift in return.

item.title: Chinese foreign minister says Beijing supports Iran’s sovereignty and security
item.description: Tehran, IRNA – China supports Iran in safeguarding its national sovereignty and security and opposes a return to military confrontation in the Middle East, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said during a meeting with Ali Bagheri, deputy secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, in Beijing on Monday.

Original source: https://en.irna.ir/news/86310431/Chinese-foreign-minister-says-Beijing-supports-Iran-s-sovereignty

item.title: Exclusive | Araghchi says Iran ‘more prepared’ for diplomacy and war; warns US to choose ‘wise path’
item.description: Ashgabat, IRNA - Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Iran is prepared for both diplomatic and military scenarios “more than ever before,” stating that the ball is now in Washington’s court to choose between a “wise path” of negotiation or repeating the “mistake of military aggression.”
item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://en.irna.ir/news/86310439/Exclusive-Araghchi-says-Iran-more-prepared-for-diplomacy

Ashgabat, IRNA - Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Iran is prepared for both diplomatic and military scenarios “more than ever before,” stating that the ball is now in Washington’s court to choose between a “wise path” of negotiation or repeating the “mistake of military aggression.”
